
# OJS and Altair Together

```{python}
#| include: false
#| label: setup
import altair as alt

import charts
import datasets
from wrangle import datacenters as dc

# Enables the vegafusion transformer and the ES-module vega renderer (required
# because the OJS cells below load RequireJS, which breaks Altair's default
# renderer — see charts/_theme.py for the full story).
charts.setup()

stats = dc.stats()
```

Quarto can support python and Observable JS (OJS) cells  in the same page. Here's a little demo:

```{python}
#| height: 600

chart = (
    alt.Chart(dc.enriched_centers()).mark_bar().encode(
        y="count():Q",
        x="Current power (MW):Q",
        color = "Owner:N"
    )
)

chart

```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

ojs_define(data = dc.enriched_centers())

```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
filtered = transpose(data).filter(function(p) {
    return p;

})
```


```{ojs}
//| title: Owner

Plot.rectY(filtered,
  Plot.binX(
    {y: "count"},
    {x: "Current power (MW)", fill: "Owner", thresholds: 20}
  ))
  .plot({
    height: 600, // Set the height explicitly - otherwise quarto dashboard doesn't render right away
    marks: [
      Plot.frame(),
    ]
  }
)
```
